# kult-atari-st-c — reimplementación de KULT (Atari ST) en C moderno

Este repositorio es la **reimplementación en C legible y documentado** del juego
*Kult: The Temple of Flying Saucers* (Exxos/ERE, 1989), hecha **a partir del
ensamblador** del decomp canónico.

## Relación con el decomp

Este repositorio parte del decomp canónico en ensamblador,
[`kult-atari-st-decomp`](https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-decomp).
El ASM es la **verdad/especificación**. Este C **no** es byte a byte (el original
fue escrito en ensamblador; ningún C da esos bytes), pero **hace lo mismo**, y eso
se comprueba con pruebas.

Este repo contiene **solo el código del core y sus pruebas**; no produce un
ejecutable jugable ni incluye material del juego original.

## Objetivo de este repo

Un **C moderno, legible, escrito a mano**, donde **cada pieza está identificada**
(nombre con sentido + comentario con su dirección original), **bien documentada**,
para que modificar el juego sea localizar la pieza y tocarla.

- Plan y método: **`docs/PLAN.md`**.
- Cómo retomar en una sesión nueva: **`AGENTS.md`**.

## Estructura

```
Makefile              compilación del candidato para pruebas + `make addrs`/`mapa`/`core`
project.toml          datos del proyecto para el arnés (nombres, base)
include/addrs.h       direcciones con nombre de los globales (GENERADO desde names.txt)
include/kult_api.h    API pública del core (frontera con el motor)
kult_core.map         version-script: exporta solo la API en el build on-target
src/                  C de la reimplementación (un módulo por subsistema)
test/                 pruebas diferenciales (harness.py + test_*.py) + convenciones
tools/recreate_kit/   arnés + oráculo (Musashi); GPL-2.0
tools/gen_addrs.py    genera include/addrs.h desde symbols/names.txt
tools/gen_mapa.py     genera docs/mapa/ desde src/, names.txt y test/
tools/regscan.py      mide la deuda de legibilidad por módulo (docs/LEGIBILIDAD.md)
symbols/              names.txt (registro de nombres)
docs/                 PROYECTOS, ESTADO, PLAN, REVISION, LEGIBILIDAD,
                      VISIBILIDAD, mapa/
```

## Estado

**Completado**: la reimplementación cubre **todo el juego**.

- `src/`: **33 módulos** (~12.620 líneas de C), **423 funciones** identificadas
  (0 placeholders) y **221 globales** con nombre.
- `test/`: **518 pruebas diferenciales** verdes contra el oráculo (Musashi),
  **0 warnings** de compilación.
- Convenciones, registro único de nombres (`names.txt`), generación de
  `addrs.h`/`docs/mapa/`, API/visibilidad on-target y **legibilidad** (0
  identificadores de registro/decompilador en código) — todo cerrado.

- Estado detallado y cómo continuar: **`docs/ESTADO.md`**.
- Plan y método: `docs/PLAN.md` · legibilidad: `docs/LEGIBILIDAD.md` ·
  visibilidad on-target: `docs/VISIBILIDAD.md`.
- La revisión del C está cerrada y la base fue **validada en Windows
  (2026-10-23)**; queda **congelada** como `core-base-20261023`
  (`docs/REVISION.md` §7/§9/§11).

## Cómo se verifica

```sh
cd kult-atari-st-c
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt   # una vez
make test            # ejecuta el diferencial contra el oráculo
```

El arnés ejecuta el **original** en el oráculo (Musashi) y compara con tu C
(memoria y registros). Si coincide, la pieza es fiel.

> **Windows:** el arnés y `make test` están pensados para Linux (o WSL). El kit
> usa `.venv/bin/python`; en Windows nativo la ruta sería
> `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` y el flujo no está soportado tal cual. Usa
> **WSL** y crea el venv dentro de WSL.

## Licencia

El código propio de este repositorio se distribuye bajo la licencia **MIT**
(ver [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). El kit de verificación
[`tools/recreate_kit`](tools/recreate_kit) se mantiene bajo **GPL-2.0**; los
detalles están en [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) y
[`LICENSES/GPL-2.0.txt`](LICENSES/GPL-2.0.txt).

El juego original sigue bajo copyright de sus respectivos titulares. Este
repositorio contiene únicamente código y no incluye material del juego.

# AGENTS.md — relevo de kult-atari-st-c

Documento de arranque para un agente que retoma el trabajo. Es el punto de
entrada; el detalle vive en `docs/`.

## Qué es este repo

Reimplementación en **C legible** de *Kult: The Temple of Flying Saucers*
(Atari ST, 1989), **fiel en comportamiento** al original.

- **Especificación congelada (no se toca):** `../kult-atari-st-decomp`
  (`matching/auto_*.s` por función, `*.s` manuales, `data_*.s`). Ensambla al
  original **byte a byte**. Las rutas `../...` asumen que el decomp está clonado
  junto a este repo.
- **Este repo:** el C, verificado con **diferencial** contra el oráculo (Musashi)
  del kit (`tools/recreate_kit`): compara memoria + registros + ledger de
  efectos off-image (paleta, PSG, IKBD…).
- Este repositorio contiene **solo código**; no produce un ejecutable jugable ni
  incluye material del juego original.

## Estado (a día de hoy)

- **Todo el juego portado:** 33 módulos, ~12.5k líneas, 518 pruebas
  diferenciales verdes, 0 warnings, `make regscan` `ids_reg=0`, `make core` OK.
- **Revisión del C: cerrada y validada.** P0 (§7), P1 (§9) y P2 (§11)
  auditados; 0 ALTA/MEDIA abiertos. Base validada en Windows (2026-10-23) y
  congelada como `core-base-20261023`. Registro completo en `docs/REVISION.md`.
- Detalle de estado y censo: `docs/ESTADO.md`.

## Método por función (resumen)

1. Abrir el `auto_*.s` de la función en
   `../kult-atari-st-decomp/matching/` (si no existe como `auto_`, buscar la
   etiqueta `f_XXXXXX` en `*.s` manuales) y comparar con el cuerpo C
   instrucción a instrucción: anchos `.b/.w/.l`, signo, banderas C/Z/N/V,
   pre/post-incremento, bucles `dbra` (¡do-while!), orden de escritura, colas
   `rts`/fall-through, registros de salida/`movem`, out-params y el ledger.
2. Registrar cada divergencia con la plantilla de `docs/REVISION.md` §5.
3. Si es un fallo real: **arreglarlo con su prueba diferencial**.
4. `make test` verde, `make regscan` `ids_reg=0`, `make core` OK.
5. Commit `revision(<módulo>): …` y `make mapa`.
6. Al cerrar una tanda: registro (§7/§9/§11), `docs/ESTADO.md`, `make mapa`.

Herramientas: `docs/mapa/<módulo>.md` (fichas), `make addrs` (si tocas
`names.txt`), `make mapa` (regenera fichas), `make regscan` (deuda de
legibilidad).

## Comandos

Desde la raíz del repo:

```sh
make test                      # ejecuta el diferencial (518)
make test PYTEST_ARGS=-n0      # serial (depuración)
make regscan                   # debe dar ids_reg=0
make core                      # build on-target con la API restringida
make mapa / make addrs         # regenerar fichas / direcciones
```

## Reglas de trabajo

- **Reproducir/medir antes de tocar.** Una hipótesis, un cambio.
- **Toda corrección deja su prueba diferencial** (salvo divergencia inobservable,
  que se marca *intencional* con justificación en el registro).
- Commit por módulo; no tocar `../kult-atari-st-decomp`.
- `make regscan` debe seguir en `ids_reg=0`. **Todo en español.**

## Documentos clave

| archivo | para qué |
|---|---|
| `docs/PROYECTOS.md` | relación entre este repo y el decomp |
| `docs/ESTADO.md` | estado exacto, censo, cómo continuar |
| `docs/REVISION.md` | plan de revisión y **registro** (§7/§9/§11) |
| `docs/PLAN.md` | plan maestro y convenciones (§4.1) |
| `docs/mapa/<módulo>.md` | ficha por módulo (funciones, globales, pruebas) |
| `docs/LEGIBILIDAD.md` | tandas de legibilidad (histórico) |
| `docs/VISIBILIDAD.md` | API pública on-target (`kult_core.map`) |

hunkstalker-kult-atari-st-c-makefile.text:
# Kult reconstruction. The shared candidate/oracle/test rules live in the kit.
KIT  := tools/recreate_kit
GAME := kult
# The toolchain here is gcc (Alpine); the kit defaults to clang.
CC   := gcc
include $(KIT)/kit.mk

# Regenera include/addrs.h desde symbols/names.txt (unica fuente de los globales).
.PHONY: addrs
addrs:
	$(PY) tools/gen_addrs.py --write

# Regenera docs/mapa/ (fichas por modulo + mapa) desde src/, names.txt y test/.
.PHONY: mapa
mapa:
	$(PY) tools/gen_mapa.py

# Mide la deuda de legibilidad por modulo (docs/LEGIBILIDAD.md).
.PHONY: regscan
regscan:
	$(PY) tools/regscan.py

# Core con la API publica restringida por version-script (build on-target).
# El build diferencial (build/libkult.so) NO usa esto: necesita todos los simbolos.
CORE     := build/libkultcore.so
CORE_SRC := $(wildcard src/*.c) $(wildcard $(KIT)/src/*.c)
$(CORE): $(CORE_SRC) $(wildcard include/*.h) kult_core.map
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -shared -Wl,--version-script=kult_core.map $(CORE_SRC) -o $(CORE)
.PHONY: core
core: $(CORE)
test: $(CORE)

hunkstalker-kult-atari-st-pc-port-readme.text:
# Kult: The Temple of Flying Saucers — Port a PC (Atari ST)

Port nativo (**Windows, Linux y macOS**) de **Kult** (Exxos/ERE, 1989), con
**español y catalán**.

![Kult Settings](assets/Kult%20Settings.png)

No parte de cero: el **C verificado** del Atari ST está importado en
`lib/kult-core/` y este repo añade un **backend de PC** (SDL3) para que ese mismo
C corra en Windows, Linux y macOS.

> **Estado:** el port es jugable de principio a fin en Windows y Linux. La
> versión **1.1.0** añade macOS Universal 2 (Intel + Apple Silicon), firmado en
> modo ad-hoc y no notarizado; la validación visual manual en Mac Intel está
> pendiente. Incluye la ingesta de los discos originales, el selector de idioma,
> los packs español y catalán, guardado/carga y audio, además de **fullscreen
> nativo**, **F1**
> ventana/fullscreen, **F2** escala Estirar a pantalla/×1–×6/Auto y **F5/F6/F7** para
> ranuras de savestate (`saves/slot-N.save`), con avisos OSD en la **fuente original del
> juego**.
> El seguimiento técnico del desarrollo está en **`PROYECTO.md`**, **`TODO.md`** y
> **`RETOMAR.md`**.

## Core importado

El núcleo vive en **`lib/kult-core/`**, importado del repo
[`kult-atari-st-c`](https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c) mediante
`git subtree`. El build usa solo `lib/kult-core/src` e `include`; el resto de
documentación, tests y herramientas del core quedan disponibles pero no se
compilan.

Los cambios propios del port dentro del core están documentados en
[`docs/CORE_DELTA.md`](docs/CORE_DELTA.md). Al actualizar el core:

```sh
git subtree pull --prefix=lib/kult-core \
  https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c.git main --squash
```

## Documentación
- **`PROYECTO.md`** — contexto maestro, arquitectura y estado.
- **`TODO.md`** — tareas pendientes / en curso / completadas.
- **`RETOMAR.md`** — handoff de sesión (qué retomar y cómo).
- **`docs/REPOSITORIO.md`** — qué se versiona y qué queda fuera.
- **`AGENTS.md`** — reglas y arranque para agentes/colaboradores.
- **`docs/INDICE.md`** — índice de toda la documentación.
- **`docs/CORE_DELTA.md`** — core importado y cambios locales del port.
- **`docs/RELEASE.md`** — formato portable, contenedores y errores de release.
- **`docs/DATA_FORMAT.md`** — formato de `kult.data`/`language.data` e ingesta STX.
- **`docs/LANGUAGE_PACKS.md`** — packs español/catalán y limitaciones de fuente.
- **`docs/TESTS.md`** — inventario y política de tests.
- **`notes/`** — notas de sesión (histórico).

## Objetivo (resumen)
- Juego nativo en C, **sin emulador** (Musashi solo se usa como oráculo en las
  pruebas del core).
- Base **Atari ST**; el trabajo sobre Amiga queda para fases posteriores.
- **Español y catalán**, además de D/E/F.
- Backend **SDL3** (ventana, entrada, audio, GPU) + renderizador planar→RGB.

## Requisitos
- **Windows 10 o superior, 64 bits**, **Linux x86_64** o **macOS 11 o superior**
  (Intel o Apple Silicon) para los paquetes precompilados. Linux y macOS también
  se pueden compilar desde el código fuente.
  Release: <https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-pc-port/releases>.
- Una copia legal del juego con los dos discos en formato `.STX`:
  `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`. Los nombres no importan; se identifican por
  SHA-256.

## Primera ejecución

El paquete no incluye el juego: necesitas `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`. En la
primera ejecución se validan los discos, se genera `data/kult.data` y el juego
continúa arrancando en esa misma ejecución. **No hace falta ejecutarlo dos
veces.** En las siguientes ejecuciones, si existe `data/kult.data`, los `.STX`
ya no son necesarios y puedes borrarlos.

En Windows y Linux no uses una carpeta de solo lectura (`Program Files`,
`/opt`): el juego escribe `data/`, `saves/`, `kult.ini` y `kult.log` junto al
ejecutable o al AppImage. En macOS escribe en Application Support.

### Windows ZIP

1. Descomprime `kult-1.1.0-win64.zip` en una carpeta escribible.
2. Copia `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX` junto a `kult.exe` o dentro de `data/`.
3. Ejecuta `kult.exe` con doble clic.
4. La primera ejecución crea `data/` y `saves/`, ingiere los discos y genera
   `data/kult.data`; al terminar, el juego arranca.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta de nuevo `kult.exe`. Si mueves el juego, mueve
   también `data/` y `saves/`.

### Linux TGZ

1. Descomprime `kult-1.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` en una carpeta escribible.
2. Copia los `.STX` junto a `kult` o dentro de `data/`.
3. Ejecuta el juego:

   ```sh
   ./kult
   ```

   Si falta el permiso de ejecución: `chmod +x kult`.

4. La primera ejecución ingiere los discos, genera `data/kult.data` y arranca
   el juego en el mismo proceso.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta otra vez `./kult`; si mueves la carpeta, mueve
   `data/` y `saves/` con ella.

### Linux AppImage

1. Copia `kult-1.1.0-x86_64.AppImage` a una carpeta escribible y dale permiso:

   ```sh
   chmod +x kult-1.1.0-x86_64.AppImage
   ```

2. Copia los `.STX` junto al AppImage. También puedes ponerlos en `data/` si ya
   existe esa carpeta.
3. Ejecuta:

   ```sh
   ./kult-1.1.0-x86_64.AppImage
   ```

4. El AppImage es un único archivo: su contenido interno es de solo lectura y se
   monta temporalmente. Al arrancar, `AppRun` crea `data/` y `saves/` junto al
   AppImage, copia `language.data` y `LEEME.txt`, ingiere los discos y arranca el
   juego en esa misma ejecución.
5. Para volver a jugar, ejecuta el mismo AppImage. Si lo mueves de carpeta,
   mueve también `data/` y `saves/`.
6. Si el sistema no tiene FUSE:

   ```sh
   ./kult-1.1.0-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run
   ```

### macOS (Universal 2)

1. Descomprime `kult-1.1.0-macos-universal.zip` o abre
   `kult-1.1.0-macos-universal.dmg` y copia `Kult.app` a una carpeta normal,
   por ejemplo `Aplicaciones` o `Escritorio`.
2. Arranca `Kult.app` con doble clic. Si macOS avisa de que no está verificada,
   usa clic derecho > **Abrir** o **Ajustes del Sistema > Privacidad y
   seguridad > Abrir igualmente**. La build es ad-hoc, no está notarizada.
3. Si no hay `kult.data`, la app pide seleccionar `Kult.STX` y `Kult (B).STX`.
   Selecciona los dos. Se copian a `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/data/`,
   se procesan y el juego arranca en esa misma ejecución.
4. Los datos y partidas quedan en `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/`. Las
   siguientes ejecuciones usan `data/kult.data` y no piden los STX.
5. **Desinstalar la app:** ciérrala y arrastra `Kult.app` a la Papelera. Los
   datos, ajustes y partidas de Application Support se conservan.
6. **Eliminación completa:** si quieres borrar también los datos y las partidas,
   haz antes copia de `saves/` y ejecuta:

   ```sh
   rm -rf "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Kult"
   ```

   Opcionalmente, si existe:

   ```sh
   rm -rf "$HOME/Library/Saved Application State/com.hunkstalker.kult.savedState"
   ```

## Controles
- **Ratón**: izquierdo/teclado = acción; derecho = acción + skip.
- **F1**: pantalla completa/ventana.
- **F2**: escala **Estirar a pantalla**, ×1–×6 o Auto; Estirar llena toda la salida.
- **F5**: muestra la ranura actual; otra pulsación mientras se ve el aviso cambia de ranura; **F6**: guarda; **F7**: carga.
- **F9/F11**: bajan/suben el volumen 10%; **F10**: silencia/restaura.
- **ESC**: cierra la ventana.
- Lista completa de atajos en `Kult Settings.txt`.

## Datos y diagnóstico
- Release **portable**: `data/` contiene los assets del usuario y `saves/` las
  escrituras del juego. En Windows y Linux TGZ viven junto al ejecutable; en el
  AppImage, junto al propio AppImage; en macOS, en
  `~/Library/Application Support/Kult/`. Las ranuras F5/F6/F7 van a
  `saves/slot-0.save`…`slot-9.save`; `kult.ini` recuerda pantalla, escala,
  ranura, volumen y silencio. La escala inicial por defecto es Estirar a
  pantalla.
- **`kult.log`** se escribe junto al ejecutable/AppImage o en Application
  Support en macOS, con timestamp. En macOS los errores fatales se muestran en
  un diálogo; en Windows/Linux van al log (salvo fallo del propio log).
  `kult-headless.exe` es solo una herramienta de desarrollo y no forma parte de
  la release.

## Origen y repos
- **`kult-atari-st-decomp`** — decomp ASM del ST, byte a byte (spec, no se toca).
- **`kult-atari-st-c`** — C verificado del ST, importado en `lib/kult-core/`.
- **`kult-atari-st-pc-port`** — este repo (el port).

Detalle en `PROYECTO.md`.

## Licencia
El código, las herramientas, la documentación y los packs de idioma del port se
distribuyen bajo licencia **MIT** (ver `LICENSE`). Los componentes de terceros
conservan sus licencias (ver `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` y `LICENSES/`).

Este repositorio no incluye el juego original. El usuario aporta su copia legal;
los assets del juego quedan **gitignored**.

CPC Mac ASM
===========

Tools to compile Amstrad CPC ASM on Mac OS X.

## Description

This set of tools contains Pasmo (Z80 compiler), iDSK (dsk manager), Sublime Text build command and AppleScript to run dsk in [Arnold](http://www.bannister.org/software/arnold.htm) emulator.
Put your source file in /asm folder, add a new build system in Sublime Text with scripts/cpc.sublime-build, add the folder with iDSK and pasmo in your $HOME/.bash_profile. 
Open your .asm file, hit cmd+B and your program will be automaticaly opened in Arnold emulator.

# DskTest (an Amstrad CPC disk drive tool)
This tool is a native Amstrad CPC tool that can help to diagnose a faulty disk drive.

Main purposes:
* Measure disk drive RPMs.
* Alignment of the head.

# Requirements
Any Amstrad CPC with a working disk drive or cassette player to load the program.
Unfortunately the latest release don't work in a 464/664 machines (yet).

Head to the Releases section to download it.

# Features
* Disk drive selection.
* Start/stop the disk drive motor.
* Search for a Sector ID on a track.
* Measure RPMs.
* Alignment of the head.

# Instructions
## Options
### Drive selection
Press 1 to discover and switch to the next available drive (A/B). Only two drives are supported.
The switch can be activated even while measuring the RPMs in realtime.

### Toggle motor
Press 2 to start/stop the motor of the selected drive.

### RPM update time
Press Q-W to increase/decrease the time taken to print the partial results of RPM measurement.

A good value is between 2-8 seconds.

### Track selection
Press A-S to select the target track that will be used for the test operations.

### Sector selection
Press Z-X to select a target Sector ID to use for the test operations.

### Test RPMs
Press ENTER (BIG Enter) to start/stop measuring the RPMs of the current selected drive. It turns the motor on, searches for an invalid Sector ID and it starts the process.

The RPM results will be calculated using the amount of seconds specified in the options.

### Test Sector ID
Press ENTER (Big enter) to search for the specified Sector ID at the specified track.

### Test head alignment
Be careful when using this test since it will run indefinitely until it succeeds.

This test will iterate from Track 0 until the selected track and will start reading all the Sector IDs for each of the tracks starting from the specified Sector ID until Sector ID+9 retrying the same Sector ID until it is found.
This will enable us to adjust in real time the alignment.
You can start specifying a low track number and progress to higher ones.

You need to ensure the disk you use contains no errors and that the specified Sector ID at the beginning of the test is the first of each track.

For an Amstrad DATA format disk that would be the Sector ID number 193 (c1 in hex)

# A bit of background
The original code and the build pipeline (python 2.7 based) is more than 10 years old but it's been modified to work with Python 3.

Surprisingly it only needed changes on the print statements and string output from the subprocess.Popen commands. The rest did work as it was.

The build script(s) expect the compiler binaries and tools to exist under specific directories and are not taken from the system PATH. The tools are provided for both MacOS and Windows so it should work without issues in any of the systems.

But right at the moment I can only ensure it works out of the box with a MacOS computer with M1/2/3/4/5 processors and using SDCC 4.5.0.

Some of the required tools like hex2bin were compiled years ago and put into the respective directories. Feel free to re-compile and/or source the binaries yourself if you don't trust the executables.

"""
IMGCONV.PY by Javier Garcia

bit 7	bit 6	bit 5	bit 4	bit 3	bit 2	bit 1	bit 0
pixel 0	pixel 1	pixel 2	pixel 3	pixel 4	pixel 5	pixel 6	pixel 7

Mode 1, 320×200, 4 colors (2 bits x pixel: bit 1 then bit 0)

class ConversionError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message):
        self.message = message

    def __str__(self):
        return self.message
    

class ImgConverter:
    def __init__(self, w, h, mode):
        self.mode = mode
        self.palette = []
        self.img = bytearray()
        self.imgw = w
        self.imgh = h
        self.hex2index = {}
        for i, rgb in enumerate(CPC_RGB_COLORS):
            self.hex2index[f'#{rgb[0]:02X}{rgb[1]:02X}{rgb[2]:02X}'] = i
                 
    def _colors_per_mode(self, mode):
        if mode == 0: return 16
        return 4 if mode == 1 else 2

    def _palette2colors(self):
        colors = []
        for hwid in self.palette:
            fwid = CPC_HW_COLORS[hwid]
            colors.append(CPC_FW_COLORS[fwid][1])
        return colors

    def _get_color_distance(self, col1, col2):
        """ colors expected as (r, g, b) values"""
        return abs(col1[0] - col2[0]) + abs(col1[1] - col2[1]) + abs(col1[2] - col2[2])
    
    def _findcolor(self, hexpixel, cpccolors):
        nearest = (999, -1)
        h = hexpixel.lstrip('#')
        rgbpixel = tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
        for i in range(0, len(cpccolors)):
            diff = (self._get_color_distance(rgbpixel, cpccolors[i]), i)
            nearest = min(nearest, diff)
        return nearest

    def _img2mode(self):
        pixelxbyte = 8 if self.mode == 2 else 4 if self.mode == 1 else 2
        totalbytes = int((self.imgh * self.imgw) / pixelxbyte)
        data = bytearray([0x00 for i in range(0, totalbytes)])
        for i in range(0, len(self.img)):
            video_byte = int(i / pixelxbyte)
            if self.mode == 2:
                pos = 7 - (i % pixelxbyte)
                data[video_byte] = data[video_byte] | (self.img[i] << pos)
            elif self.mode == 1:
                pos = 3 - (i % pixelxbyte)
                data[video_byte] = data[video_byte] | (self.img[i] & 0x02) << (pos+3) | (self.img[i] & 0x01) << pos
            else:
                pos = 1 - (i % pixelxbyte)
                data[video_byte] = data[video_byte] | \
                             (self.img[i] & 0x01) << (6 + pos) | \
                             (self.img[i] & 0x02) << (1 + pos) | \
                             (self.img[i] & 0x04) << (2 + pos) | \
                             (self.img[i] & 0x08) >> (3 - pos)
        return data

    def _build_palette(self, sprite):
        """
        Assigns each pixel in the image to a CPC color. When
        all pixels are assigned, the method retains the colors with more
        assignements and builds the palette. The mode sets the max number
        of allowed entries.
        """
        ocurrences = [(0, i) for i in range(0, len(CPC_RGB_COLORS))]
        for row in range(self.imgh):
            for col in range(self.imgw):
                pixel = sprite[self.imgw * row + col][1]
                index = self.hex2index[pixel]
                ocurrences[index] = (ocurrences[index][0] + 1, index)
        palette = list(filter(lambda item: item[0] > 0, ocurrences))
        palette.sort(reverse=True)
        colors = self._colors_per_mode(self.mode)
        self.palette = list(map(lambda item: CPC_FW_COLORS[item[1]][0], palette[0:colors]))

    def _build_cpcimg(self, sprite):
        """
        Convert each RGB value to a CPC HW color value included in the
        palette. If more colors that allowed were used, the method selects
        the nearest valid color.
        """
        self._build_palette(sprite)
        palettecolors = self._palette2colors()
        self.img = bytearray()
        for y in range(0, self.imgh):
            for x in range(0, self.imgw):
                pixel = sprite[self.imgw * y + x][1]
                _, colorindex = self._findcolor(pixel, palettecolors)
                self.img.extend(colorindex.to_bytes(1, 'little'))
        
    def code_c(self, sprite, name):
        self._build_cpcimg(sprite)
        data = self._img2mode()
        code = []
        strpalette = '{ %s }' % ', '.join('0x%02X' % x for x in self.palette)
        code.append("// C format sprite created with Tixel\n")
        code.append(f"// mode {self.mode}, width {self.imgw}, height {self.imgh}\n\n")
        code.append(f"const unsigned char {name.upper()}_PAL[{len(self.palette)}] = {strpalette};\n\n")
        code.append(f"const unsigned char {name.upper()}_IMG[{len(sprite)}] = {{\n")
        pixbyte = 8 if self.mode == 2 else 4 if self.mode == 1 else 2
        row = min(16, int(self.imgw / pixbyte))
        while len(data) > 0:
            line = data[0:row]
            end = ',\n' if len(data) > row else '\n'
            code.append('    ' + ', '.join('0x%02X' % x for x in line) + end)
            data = data[row:]
        code.append('};\n')
        return code
        

    def code_asm(self, sprite, name):
        self._build_cpcimg(sprite)
        data = self._img2mode()
        code = []
        strpalette = ', '.join('0x%02X' % x for x in self.palette)
        code.append("; Assembly format sprite created with Tixel\n")
        code.append(f"; mode {self.mode}, width {self.imgw}, height {self.imgh}\n\n")
        code.append(f"{name.lower()}_pal:\n")
        code.append(f"\tdb {strpalette}\n\n")
        code.append(f"{name.lower()}_img:\n")
        pixbyte = 8 if self.mode == 2 else 4 if self.mode == 1 else 2
        row = min(16, int(self.imgw / pixbyte))
        while len(data) > 0:
            line = data[0:row]
            code.append('\tdb ' + ', '.join('&%02X' % x for x in line) + '\n')
            data = data[row:]
        code.append('\n')
        return code
        
    def code_bas(self, sprite, name):
        if name == "": name = "unnamed"
        self._build_cpcimg(sprite)
        code = []
        strpalette = ': '.join('INK %d,%d' % (i,CPC_HW_COLORS[x]) for i,x in enumerate(self.palette))
        code.append("10 ' BASIC formated sprite created with Tixel\n")
        code.append(f"20 ' {name}: mode {self.mode}, width {self.imgw}, height {self.imgh}\n")
        code.append("30 ' Palette:\n")
        code.append(f"40 ' {strpalette} \n")
        code.append("50 ' \n")
        xcursors = int(self.imgw / 8)
        ycursors = int(self.imgh / 8)
        symbols = 256 - (len(self.palette) * xcursors * ycursors)
        code.append(f"60 SYMBOL AFTER {symbols}\n")
        # I know, I know... the next code is not very elegant
        line = 70
        for cindex in range(0,len(self.palette)):
            code.append(f"{line} ' Symbol definitions for INK {cindex}\n")
            line = line + 10
            for y in range(0, ycursors):
                for x in range(0, xcursors):
                    symbol = []
                    for cline in range(0, 8):  # a cursor has 8 lines
                        imgpos = (x * 8) + (self.imgw * (y * 8 + cline))
                        symval = 0
                        symval = symval + (128 if self.img[imgpos] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (64 if self.img[imgpos+1] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (32 if self.img[imgpos+2] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (16 if self.img[imgpos+3] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (8 if self.img[imgpos+4] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (4 if self.img[imgpos+5] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (2 if self.img[imgpos+6] == cindex else 0)
                        symval = symval + (1 if self.img[imgpos+7] == cindex else 0)
                        symbol.append(symval)
                    code.append(f"{line} SYMBOL {symbols}")
                    line = line + 10
                    for v in symbol: code.append(f",{v}")
                    code.append("\n")
                    symbols = symbols + 1
        return code

# Mini DAAD Linux

🇪🇸 [Lee este documento en español](LEEME.md)

This is a collection of scripts and tools that allow you to build
text adventures natively for retro computers such as the ZX Spectrum,
Amstrad CPC, Commodore 64, and several others, using the DAAD interpreters.

It is based on [DAAD Ready](https://www.ngpaws.com/daadready/index.html).

The rest of this document assumes that you are already familiar with
creating adventures using this system. If not, we recommend reading the
**DAAD Ready** documentation before continuing.

## License

The **scripts developed specifically for Mini DAAD Linux**
are distributed under the license:

> **GNU General Public License v2 or later (GPL v2+)**

However, this project makes use of tools, utilities, and
components developed by third parties.

Each of these elements may be subject to **its own license**. Users
should check the licensing conditions on each tool's official website.

Some external tools used:

 * [DRC](https://github.com/Utodev/DRC)
 * [PCDAAD](https://github.com/Utodev/PCDAAD)
 * [MALUVA](https://github.com/Utodev/MALUVA)
 * [ZX0](https://github.com/einar-saukas/ZX0)
 * [CPCXfs](https://www.octoate.de/download/cpcxfs/)
 * [DSKTOOL](https://github.com/lvitals/dsktool)

## Dependencies

* In order to run the scripts, **PHP** must be installed.
  To generate HTML games, the **php-gd** extension is also required.

* If you want to create a game for Commodore 64, you must install
  the **VICE** emulator, since the scripts use one of its utilities
  to create the game disk.

* For MSX2, **Python 3** with the **NumPy** library is also required.

You will also need several emulators if you want to test your game.
The emulators to be used can be configured in the `config.sh` file.

### Recommended emulators

Some emulators are usually included in Linux distributions,
so they are easy to install (although you may need to locate
and install the ROMs for the machines).

- [Fuse](https://fuse-emulator.sourceforge.net), an emulator for ZX Spectrum machines.
- [Vice](https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io), an emulator for Commodore machines.
- [Dosbox](https://www.dosbox.com), an MS-DOS emulator.
- [OpenMSX](https://openmsx.org), an emulator for MSX1 and MSX2.
  It requires the ROMs `nms8250_basic-bios2.rom`, `nms8250_disk.rom`, and `nms8250_msx2sub.rom`.
- [ZEsarUX](https://github.com/chernandezba/zesarux), emulates several machines,
  including traditional ZX Spectrum models, the newer ZX Spectrum Next,
  and others such as the Amstrad CPC 6128.

## Supported platforms

Currently, Mini DAAD Linux can compile games for the following platforms:

- ZX Spectrum 48K (no graphics)
- ZX Spectrum 128K
- ZX Spectrum +3
- ZX Spectrum Next
- Amstrad CPC 6128
- Commodore 64
- MSX 1
- MSX 2
- MS-DOS
- HTML (playable in web browsers)

## How to use

The procedure to compile a game for a specific machine is as follows:

1) Place the `.dsf` file containing the game source code in the same
   directory as the scripts.  
   If you do not have a `.dsf` file, running one of the scripts will
   create a sample file.

2) Edit the `config.sh` file and set **GAME** to the name of the game
   (it must match the name of the `.dsf` file without the `.dsf` extension).

3) Place the images in the `IMAGES` folder as explained in the [Multimedia](#multimedia) section.

4) Run one of the following scripts, which will compile the game:

    | Script             | Platform            |
    |--------------------|--------------------|
    | `zx48k.sh`         | ZX Spectrum 48K    |
    | `zx128k.sh`        | ZX Spectrum 128K   |
    | `zxplus3.sh`       | ZX Spectrum +3     |
    | `zxnext.sh`        | ZX Spectrum Next   |
    | `c64.sh`           | Commodore 64       |
    | `cpc6128.sh`       | Amstrad CPC 6128   |
    | `msx1.sh`          | MSX 1             |
    | `msx2.sh`          | MSX 2             |
    | `msdos.sh`         | MS-DOS             |
    | `html.sh`          | HTML               |

If compilation succeeds and the corresponding emulator is installed, the
game will launch automatically.

The generated files can be found inside the `RELEASE` directory.

## Multimedia

Images for each platform must be placed in the following directories:

| Platform                  | Format        | Resolution | Folder            |
|---------------------------|--------------|------------|-------------------|
| ZX Spectrum               | `.scr`       | 256x192    | `IMAGES`          |
| Amstrad CPC (mode 0)      | `.scr`/`.pal`| 160x200    | `IMAGES/CPC`      |
| Amstrad CPC (mode 1)      | `.scr`/`.pal`| 320x200    | `IMAGES/CPC`      |
| ZX Spectrum Next          | `.pcx`       | 256x192    | `IMAGES`          |
| Commodore 64 (HiRes)      | `.art`       | 320x200    | `IMAGES`          |
| Commodore 64 (Multicolor) | `.koa`       | 160x200    | `IMAGES`          |
| MSX 1                     | `.sc2`       | 256x192    | `IMAGES`          |
| MSX 2                     | `.sc8`       | 256x212    | `IMAGES`          |
| MS-DOS (VGA)              | `.pcx`       | 320x200    | `IMAGES/PC`       |
| MS-DOS (SVGA)             | `.pcx`       | 640x400    | `IMAGES/PC/SVGA`  |
| HTML                      | `.png`       | 320x200    | `IMAGES/HTML`     |

Videos must be placed in:

| Platform       | Format | Resolution | Folder            |
|----------------|--------|------------|-------------------|
| MS-DOS (VGA)   | `.fli` | 320x200    | `IMAGES/PC`       |
| MS-DOS (SVGA)  | `.fli` | 320x200    | `IMAGES/PC/SVGA`  |
| HTML           | `.mp4` | 320x200    | `IMAGES/HTML`     |

Sounds:

| Platform | Format | Folder   |
|----------|--------|----------|
| MS-DOS   | `.wav` | `SOUNDS` |
| HTML     | `.mp3` | `SOUNDS` |

## The `config.sh` configuration file

The `config.sh` file allows you to define compilation options
for the game, as well as configure the emulators to run it.

### Game options

* `GAME`  
  Name of the game. It must match the name of the `.dsf` file without the extension.

* `SPLITSCR` (`splitModeOff` / `splitModeOn`)

gufranco-sms-rom-image-python-readme-md.text:
# SMS ROM Image

A Sega Master System, Game Gear or SG-1000 cartridge image read as a file, held to Sega's Mark III reference manual where it speaks and to the export boot programs and 2,922 real images where it does not.

English | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-Hans.md) | [繁體中文（香港）](README.zh-HK.md)

[![CI](https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python)](https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python/releases)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

**2,922** distinct images measured from **5,425** archive entries, **0** property failures, the header read at `0x7FF0` on **2,453** of them, the stored checksum reproduced on **370** of **393** retail Master System cartridges, **14** boot programs declared by digest, **791** tests, **100%** statement and branch coverage, no dependencies

```python
from smsimage import dump, header

image = bytearray(0x8000)
image[0x7FF0:0x7FF8] = b"TMR SEGA"
image[0x7FFF] = 0x4C
image[0x7FFA:0x7FFC] = header.checksum(bytes(image)).to_bytes(2, "little")

stubbed = bytes(512) + bytes(image)
cartridge = dump.strip_copier_stub(stubbed)

print(dump.form(stubbed), len(cartridge))
print(
    hex(header.anchor_of(cartridge)), header.region_of(cartridge), header.declared_size(cartridge)
)
print(header.agrees(cartridge))
```

```
stubbed 32768
0x7ff0 sms-export 32768
True
```

The example builds a 32K image with a header at `0x7FF0`, writes region and size byte `0x4C`, and seals the checksum this package computes into the two checksum bytes. It then puts a 512-byte copier block in front. `strip_copier_stub` recognises the block by the length alone and removes it. The header reads back as an export Master System cartridge declaring 32K, and the stored checksum matches the computed one.

## Install

| Requirement | Version       |
| :---------- | :------------ |
| Python      | 3.12 or newer |
| git         | Any, to clone |

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python.git
cd sms-rom-image-python
python3 smsimage/doctor.py
```

The package imports nothing outside the standard library. There is no submodule, so a plain clone and the download-zip link both give a checkout that runs. `pip install git+https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python.git` installs the package alone, with the doctor as the `smsimage-doctor` command.

The doctor checks the machine and the checkout and ends with one line. Paste its whole output into any bug report.

```
  9 checks, nothing to report
```

Releases follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and are cut from the commit history by semantic-release. Every release is tagged and listed on the [releases page](https://github.com/gufranco/sms-rom-image-python/releases).

## The interface

Four modules answer four questions, in the order a caller has to ask them.

| Module                             | Question                                                 |
| :--------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`dump`](smsimage/dump.py)         | What did the dumping device add                          |
| [`header`](smsimage/header.py)     | What does the cartridge say about itself, and where      |
| [`identity`](smsimage/identity.py) | What makes this file itself, and which value decides     |
| [`manifest`](smsimage/manifest.py) | When a reader supplies the wrong file, which wrong is it |

Every query on an image answers `None` rather than raising when there is nothing to read. A missing header is a normal state: 456 of the 2,922 images carry none.

### Reading a dump

| Call                           | Returns                                                                                                                    |
| :----------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dump.read(path)`              | The file's bytes with a copier block removed when there is one. `path` is a `str` or a `Path`                              |
| `dump.form(data)`              | `"stubbed"` when `data` is longer than 512 bytes and its length leaves 512 over a whole number of kilobytes, else `"bare"` |
| `dump.strip_copier_stub(data)` | `data` without its first 512 bytes when the form is `"stubbed"`, else `data` unchanged                                     |

```python
from smsimage import dump

for length in (512, 1536, 32768, 33280):
    print(length, dump.form(bytes(length)), len(dump.strip_copier_stub(bytes(length))))
```

```
512 bare 512
1536 stubbed 1024
32768 bare 32768
33280 stubbed 32768
```

The test is the length and nothing else. A 512-byte file is bare because nothing would be left behind the block. `dump.read` has already stripped the block, so to ask which form a file was in, read the bytes yourself and pass them to `dump.form`.

### The header

| Call                          | Returns                                                                                                                 |
| :---------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `header.anchors_in(image)`    | Every candidate offset holding `TMR SEGA`, largest first, as a tuple                                                    |
| `header.anchor_of(image)`     | The first of those, or `None`                                                                                           |
| `header.region_of(image)`     | The name for the high nibble of the byte at anchor plus `0x0F`, or `None` when no header or no name                     |
| `header.declared_size(image)` | The size in bytes for the low nibble of that byte, or `None` when no header or a code the reading does not know         |
| `header.carried(image)`       | The little-endian word at anchor plus `0x0A`, or `None` with no header                                                  |
| `header.checksum(image)`      | The sum the export boot program computes, as an `int` below `0x10000`, or `None` with no header or an unknown size code |
| `header.agrees(image)`        | `checksum(image) == carried(image)`, or `None` when there is no checksum to compare                                     |

```python
from smsimage import header

image = bytearray(0x8000)
image[0x7FF0:0x7FF8] = b"TMR SEGA"
image[0x7FFA:0x7FFC] = (0x1234).to_bytes(2, "little")

for nibbles in (0x6C, 0x9C, 0x63):
    image[0x7FFF] = nibbles
    held = bytes(image)
    print(
        hex(nibbles),
        header.region_of(held),
        header.declared_size(held),
        hex(header.carried(held)),
        header.checksum(held),
        header.agrees(held),
    )

print(header.region_of(bytes(0x8000)), header.carried(bytes(0x8000)), header.agrees(b""))
```

```
0x6c gg-export 32768 0x1234 0 False
0x9c None 32768 0x1234 0 False
0x63 gg-export None 0x1234 None None
None None None
```

Region nibble 9 has no name, so `region_of` answers `None` while the size still reads. Size nibble 3 has no entry in the table, so there is no span to sum and no checksum to compare. An image with no header answers `None` to every query, and so does an empty one.

### Identity

| Call                               | Returns                                                                                              |
| :--------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `identity.measure(data)`           | A mapping of `size`, `crc32`, `md5`, `sha1` and `sha256`, the digests as lowercase hex               |
| `identity.agrees(found, expected)` | Whether the two `sha256` values match, ignoring case. Raises `NoAuthority` when either side has none |

One value decides whether a file is the file, and a record whose weaker values disagree still matches when that one agrees:

```python
from smsimage import identity

found = identity.measure(b"cartridge")
record = {"sha256": found["sha256"], "crc32": "00000000", "size": 1}

print(identity.AUTHORITATIVE)
print(identity.agrees(found, record))
```

```
sha256
True
```

A record carrying no SHA-256 is refused rather than graded on whichever weaker value it carries:

```python
from smsimage import NoAuthority, identity

try:
    identity.agrees(identity.measure(b"cartridge"), {"crc32": "e9648752"})
except NoAuthority as error:
    print(error)
```

```
nothing decides: no sha256 to compare
```

### Manifests

`Manifest(document)` takes a mapping with an `artifacts` mapping. Each artifact has an `accepted` list of records, each carrying `sha256`, and may carry a `name` and a `badDumps` list whose entries carry `sha256` and `why`. `manifest.read(path)` parses a JSON file into one.

| Member                       | Meaning                                                             |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Manifest.keys`              | The artifact keys, as a tuple                                       |
| `Manifest.name(key)`         | The artifact's `name`, or `key` when it has none or is not declared |
| `Manifest.match(key, data)`  | A `Match` for the bytes `data` against artifact `key`               |
| `Match.key`, `Match.verdict` | The key asked about and one of the five verdicts below              |
| `Match.found`                | What `identity.measure` returned for the bytes                      |
| `Match.why`                  | The `why` of the bad dump matched, else `None`                      |
| `bool(match)`                | True only for `accepted`                                            |

| Verdict                               | When                                                        |
| :------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `accepted`                            | The SHA-256 is one the artifact accepts                     |
| `a known bad dump`                    | The SHA-256 is one the artifact lists under `badDumps`      |
| `the right length, the wrong content` | The size matches an accepted record and the digest does not |
| `a length nothing declares`           | Neither the digest nor the size matches                     |
| `undeclared`                          | The manifest has no artifact under that key                 |

```python
from smsimage import Manifest, identity

boot = bytes(8192)
expected = identity.measure(boot)

record = Manifest({"artifacts": {"bios": {"name": "a boot program", "accepted": [dict(expected)]}}})

print(record.match("bios", boot).verdict)
print(record.match("bios", bytes(8191) + b"\x01").verdict)
print(record.match("bios", bytes(4096)).verdict)
print(record.match("cartridge", boot).verdict)
```

```
accepted
the right length, the wrong content
a length nothing declares
undeclared
```

A known bad dump is declared apart from the accepted files, so a corrupt copy is diagnosed as corrupt rather than as the wrong file. A document that is not a manifest is refused when it is built:

```python
from smsimage import Malformed, Manifest, NoAuthority, identity

good = bytes(8192)
corrupt = bytes(8190) + b"\xff\xff"
record = Manifest(
    {
        "artifacts": {
            "bios": {
                "name": "a boot program",
                "accepted": [dict(identity.measure(good))],
                "badDumps": [{"sha256": identity.measure(corrupt)["sha256"], "why": "last word"}],
            }
        }
    }
)

found = record.match("bios", corrupt)
print(record.keys, record.name("bios"), record.name("cartridge"))
print(found, bool(found), found.why, found.found["size"])
print(bool(record.match("bios", good)))

for document in ([], {"artifacts": {}}, {"artifacts": {"bios": {"accepted": [{"size": 1}]}}}):
    try:
        Manifest(document)
    except (Malformed, NoAuthority) as error:
        print(type(error).__name__, error)
```

```
('bios',) a boot program cartridge
<Match bios: a known bad dump> False last word 8192
True
Malformed a manifest is a mapping, and this is not one
Malformed a manifest declares artifacts, and this declares none
NoAuthority bios: an accepted file with no sha256 to decide on
```

### Errors

Both live in [`smsimage/errors.py`](smsimage/errors.py) and are published at the top of the package, so a caller can catch each by name.

| Error         | Raised when                                                                                                                                                             |
| :------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Malformed`   | `Manifest` is given something that is not a mapping, declares no artifacts, has an artifact that is not a mapping, or has one whose `accepted` list is missing or empty |
| `NoAuthority` | `identity.agrees` is given a side with no `sha256`, or `Manifest` is given an accepted record with none                                                                 |

`manifest.read` lets an unreadable file or invalid JSON raise what `pathlib` and `json` raise.

### Module contents

| Name                                               | Content                                                                                                                     |
| :------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smsimage.MAGIC`                                   | `b"TMR SEGA"`, the eight bytes a header opens with                                                                          |
| `smsimage.CANDIDATES`                              | `(0x7FF0, 0x3FF0, 0x1FF0)`, the offsets searched, largest first                                                             |
| `smsimage.REGIONS`                                 | Region nibble to name: `0x3` `sms-japan`, `0x4` `sms-export`, `0x5` `gg-japan`, `0x6` `gg-export`, `0x7` `gg-international` |
| `smsimage.SIZES`                                   | Size nibble to bytes: `0xA` 8K, `0xB` 16K, `0xC` 32K, `0xD` 48K, `0xE` 64K, `0xF` 128K, `0x0` 256K, `0x1` 512K, `0x2` 1M    |
| `smsimage.BARE`, `smsimage.STUBBED`                | The two values `dump.form` returns                                                                                          |
| `smsimage.AUTHORITATIVE`                           | `"sha256"`, the one value that decides                                                                                      |
| `smsimage.VERDICTS`                                | The five verdicts, in the order `match` tries them                                                                          |
| `smsimage.Manifest`, `smsimage.Match`              | The manifest and its answer                                                                                                 |
| `smsimage.Malformed`, `smsimage.NoAuthority`       | The two errors                                                                                                              |
| `smsimage.__version__`                             | The installed version                                                                                                       |
| `dump.COPIER_BLOCK`                                | 512                                                                                                                         |
| `identity.CROSS_REFERENCE`                         | `("size", "crc32", "md5", "sha1")`, measured and never deciding                                                             |
| `header.CHECKSUM`, `header.REGION_AND_SIZE`        | Where the checksum word and the region and size byte sit, relative to the anchor: `0x0A` to `0x0B`, and `0x0F`              |
| `header.FIRST_SPAN`, `header.BANKS_FROM_THE_THIRD` | The export boot program's two tables, keyed by size nibble                                                                  |

```python
import smsimage

print(smsimage.MAGIC, [hex(one) for one in smsimage.CANDIDATES])
print({hex(code): name for code, name in smsimage.REGIONS.items()})
print({hex(code): size // 1024 for code, size in smsimage.SIZES.items()})
print(smsimage.BARE, smsimage.STUBBED, smsimage.AUTHORITATIVE)
print(smsimage.VERDICTS)
```

```
b'TMR SEGA' ['0x7ff0', '0x3ff0', '0x1ff0']
{'0x3': 'sms-japan', '0x4': 'sms-export', '0x5': 'gg-japan', '0x6': 'gg-export', '0x7': 'gg-international'}
{'0x0': 256, '0x1': 512, '0x2': 1024, '0xa': 8, '0xb': 16, '0xc': 32, '0xd': 48, '0xe': 64, '0xf': 128}
bare stubbed sha256
('accepted', 'a known bad dump', 'the right length, the wrong content', 'a length nothing declares', 'undeclared')
```

### The doctor

`python3 smsimage/doctor.py`, or `smsimage-doctor` after a pip install, takes no arguments. It reports on the machine: the interpreter, the output and default encodings, filesystem case, line endings, path length, free space and git. It then drives the package against an image it assembles: it strips a copier block, finds a planted header, reproduces a sealed checksum, measures the image, parses [`artifacts.manifest.json`](artifacts.manifest.json) and reads [`conformance/corpus.json`](conformance/corpus.json). A corpus holding nothing is reported apart from a corpus that is not there. It exits 0 when all 9 package checks pass and 1 otherwise.

## What a real library actually contains

Sega's _Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console_ prints the header on its page 22, and [`conformance/hardware.json`](conformance/hardware.json) holds every fact it states with the sentence it came from. It is a retyped copy whose typist is not recorded. Where it and the cartridges disagree the cartridges win, and [`conformance/divergences.json`](conformance/divergences.json) carries each disagreement with its measurement. Every figure below was measured across the Master System, Game Gear and SG-1000 libraries the census was run on, keyed on the SHA-256 of the image bytes, so a count is a count of images rather than of filenames.

| Measurement                                            | Count |
| :----------------------------------------------------- | ----: |
| Archive entries read                                   | 5,425 |
| Distinct images                                        | 2,922 |
| Duplicate listings of an image already seen            | 2,503 |
| Header at `0x7FF0` only                                | 2,450 |
| Header at `0x3FF0` / `0x1FF0`                          | 8 / 5 |
| Header at both `0x3FF0` and `0x7FF0`, read at `0x7FF0` |     3 |
| No header at any candidate offset                      |   456 |
| Carrying a 512-byte copier block                       |    17 |

Five things in there break a reader written from a description.

**A header is not universal.** 456 images carry none, and only 76 of those are too short to hold one at `0x7FF0`. 205 of them are the retail SG-1000 cartridges, none of which carries a header: they are the control that catches a header finder saying yes to everything. So every query answers `None` rather than raising.

**The magic appears where no header is.** Read as raw files, 141 images carry `TMR SEGA` outside the three candidate offsets. 16 of those are copier-blocked images whose header sits at `0x81F0` until the block is removed. The rest sit at bank boundaries, which is what a multi-cart or an overdump looks like. Only the three candidates are searched.

**Three images carry the magic at two candidates.** The largest wins, and `anchors_in` reports every match so a caller sees the ambiguity.

```python
from smsimage import header

image = bytearray(0x40000)
image[0x3FF0:0x3FF8] = b"TMR SEGA"
image[0x7FF0:0x7FF8] = b"TMR SEGA"

print([hex(one) for one in header.anchors_in(bytes(image))])
print(hex(header.anchor_of(bytes(image))))
print(header.anchor_of(bytes(0x8000)))
```

```
['0x7ff0', '0x3ff0']
0x7ff0
None
```

**The two bytes after the magic are not reserved.** The manual prints them as two spaces, `20 20`, and only 400 of the 2,466 headers carry them. `00 00` appears on 1,149 and `FF FF` on 527, with a long tail after that. The export and Game Gear boot programs both compare eight bytes, `TMR SEGA`, and so does this package. `python3 -m conformance.divergences <library>` measures these.

**A Game Gear cartridge usually stores no checksum.** Of the 1,105 distinct images in the Game Gear set that carry a header, 1,018 store the value zero and 48 reproduce the rule, as `python3 -m conformance.divergences` measures over that set alone. The Game Gear boot program looks for `TMR SEGA` at the three addresses and checks nothing else, so nothing on that console ever read the stored value. `header.agrees` answers `False` for those, and that is a statement about the console rather than about the file.

The manual prints the size codes up to 256K, each with region nibble `0x4`. The export boot program decodes nine size codes, 512K and 1M among them, and checks the sum only on region `0x4`. The other region nibbles are named the way the emulation community names them, which no Sega document confirms. The census agrees with that naming: region `0x4` dominates the Master System images and `0x5` to `0x7` the Game Gear ones. 49 images carry a region nibble no reading accounts for and 3 a size nibble, and those resolve to `None` rather than to the nearest plausible value.

## The checksum rule

The rule is the one the export boot programs run, read out of the v1.3 program declared in [`artifacts.manifest.json`](artifacts.manifest.json). Each size code names a first span, `0x1FF0`, `0x3FF0`, `0x7FF0` or, for 48K, `0xBFF0`, and the bytes below it are summed. From 64K up, whole 16K banks from the third onward are added: 2 for 64K, 6 for 128K, 14 for 256K, 30 for 512K and 62 for 1M. The low sixteen bits are kept. `python3 -m conformance.boot <program> [program ...]` reads both tables, the eight-byte compare and the region gate out of each declared program that runs the sum and checks them against this package. Nine do, and all nine read the same first spans and the same bank counts up to 512K. For 1M they split: v1.3 and five others read 62 banks, while Hang On v3.4, Hang On & Safari Hunt v2.4 and Missile Defense 3-D v4.4 read 33, and no image in the library tells the two apart. The manual says to leave out only the two checksum bytes, and that reading reproduces the stored value on none of the 2,463 images.

| Population                                                                                                                |     Reproduced |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------: |
| Retail Master System cartridges, the four region folders of the Master System set, by `python3 -m conformance.categories` |     370 of 393 |
| Every image in the Master System set with a header and a size the reading knows, modified ones included                   |   925 of 1,331 |
| Every image with a header and a size the reading knows                                                                    | 1,011 of 2,463 |

A modified image disagrees for a reason that belongs to the modification: translations reproduce the rule on 78 of 301 and hacks on 33 of 129, as `python3 -m conformance.categories` measures. That is why the census reports agreement as an observation rather than gating on it.

No other boot program explains the 23 retail cartridges that do not reproduce. 16 of them carry a region nibble other than `0x4`, and none of the nine programs checks the sum on those. The other 7 declare 32K, 128K or 256K, where all nine read the same table.

## The census, and why its output can ship

[`conformance/census.py`](conformance/census.py) walks a library you own: directories, zip archives and single `.sms`, `.gg` and `.sg` files.

```bash
python3 -m conformance.census /path/to/library.zip /path/to/another
```

It counts each distinct image once by SHA-256, checks six properties on every one, reports one observation, and writes [`conformance/corpus.json`](conformance/corpus.json): 151 combinations of form, length, anchor, region, declared size and whether the stored checksum reproduced, each with a count. No title and no content, so nothing in it could rebuild any part of any cartridge.

| Exit code | When                                             |
| :-------- | :----------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | Every property held on every image               |
| 1         | A property broke, or a path given does not exist |
| 2         | No path was given                                |

The six properties are invariants between functions that agree by construction today. Each test replaces one side of the pair it guards and watches the property fire, so all six have been seen to catch the drift they exist for.

Given no image, the census says it examined nothing and leaves the existing corpus alone rather than overwriting it with an empty one.

## Is it right

Every fact the manual prints that a test can reach is held to the code. [`conformance/hardware.json`](conformance/hardware.json) carries each fact with its sentence and page, and [`conformance/hardware.test.py`](conformance/hardware.test.py) compares them with the constants in the package. `python3 -m conformance.quotes` finds every quoted sentence in the manual, once `python3 -m conformance.documents` has fetched it.

`python3 -m conformance.corpus` replays the 151 combinations in [`conformance/corpus.json`](conformance/corpus.json) against the package with no library present, and the suite checks the headline counts against that file. `python3 -m conformance.speed` holds the checksum of a 256K image to a floor of 130 per second.

The boot programs a reader may need are declared in [`artifacts.manifest.json`](artifacts.manifest.json) by size, CRC32, SHA-1 and SHA-256. None of them is in this repository and nothing here says where to obtain one. [OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) lists the 3 things no Sega source settles, and what would settle each.

## Working on it

| Need                                                            | Where                                                                    |
| :-------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------- |

```bash

"${cov[@]}" erase
for f in $(find smsimage conformance -name '*.test.py' | sort); do
  "${cov[@]}" run -a "$f" || echo "FAILED $f"
done
"${cov[@]}" report
```

# CMake del ejecutable del port (M7/T-070, macOS T-136). El core no se toca:
# este build enlaza lib/kult-core/src (juego) + boot/ + platform/ + app/, con
# `platform/include` el primero para sombrear os.h/hw.h/psg.h/sched.h con la HAL
# de PC. El Makefile sigue siendo el build del core y del diferencial (`make test`).
#
#   Linux:  cmake -S . -B build-linux -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ...
#   Windows (cross MinGW): ver cmake/mingw-w64.cmake y docs/BUILD.md.
#   macOS Universal 2: ver docs/BUILD.md y tools/build_macos.sh.
#
# Targets: `kult` (headless) y `kult-sdl` (ventana/audio SDL3). En Windows,
# `kult-sdl` sale como kult.exe y el headless como kult-headless.exe. En macOS,
# `kult-sdl` produce Kult.app.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET)
  set(CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET "11.0" CACHE STRING "Minimum macOS version")
endif()
project(kult VERSION 1.1.0 LANGUAGES C)

# Ruta a la SDL3 compartida que se empaqueta en Linux/macOS (se puede pasar con
# -DKULT_SDL3_LIB=...). En Windows se usa third_party/SDL3-.../SDL3.dll.
set(KULT_SDL3_LIB "" CACHE FILEPATH "SDL3 shared library to bundle on Linux/macOS")

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

# ---- fuentes (espejo de PORT_SRC del Makefile) ------------------------------
file(GLOB KULT_CORE_SRC     CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/src/*.c)
file(GLOB KULT_BOOT_SRC     CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/boot/*.c)
file(GLOB KULT_PLATFORM_SRC CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/*.c)
# La entrada/salida SDL (ventana/audio) sólo va al target `kult-sdl`; la copia
# de traza T-073c no se compila en el build estándar. Con KULT_DIAG_TRACE=ON
# se sustituye lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c por platform/dispatch_trace.c: escribe Y/V de
# todo el guion (sin depender de F12) para diagnosticar una run completa.
option(KULT_DIAG_TRACE "Usar dispatch_trace.c (traza Y/V completa)" OFF)
list(REMOVE_ITEM KULT_PLATFORM_SRC
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/video_sdl.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/audio_sdl.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/mac_dialog.c
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/dispatch_trace.c)
if(KULT_DIAG_TRACE)
  list(REMOVE_ITEM KULT_CORE_SRC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c)
  list(APPEND KULT_PLATFORM_SRC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/dispatch_trace.c)
endif()

# T-073b: solo el core se instrumenta para cobrar el coste medido por función.
# El diferencial (make test) no usa este CMake y sigue sin instrumentar.
set_source_files_properties(${KULT_CORE_SRC}
  PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-finstrument-functions")

add_library(kultport STATIC ${KULT_CORE_SRC} ${KULT_BOOT_SRC} ${KULT_PLATFORM_SRC})
# `platform/include` PRIMERO: sombrea os.h/hw.h/psg.h/sched.h del kit.
target_include_directories(kultport PUBLIC
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform/include
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/platform
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/boot
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/include
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/kult-core/tools/recreate_kit/include)
target_compile_options(kultport PRIVATE -O2 -Wall -Wextra)
target_compile_definitions(kultport PUBLIC KULT_VERSION="${PROJECT_VERSION}")
if(WIN32)
  # platform/log.c usa GetConsoleWindow/MessageBoxA (diagnóstico visible).
  target_link_libraries(kultport PUBLIC user32)
endif()

# ---- ejecutables ------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(kult app/main.c)
target_link_libraries(kult PRIVATE kultport)

add_executable(kult-sdl app/main.c platform/video_sdl.c platform/audio_sdl.c)
target_compile_definitions(kult-sdl PRIVATE HAVE_SDL3)
target_include_directories(kult-sdl PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets)
if(APPLE)
  target_sources(kult-sdl PRIVATE platform/mac_dialog.c)
endif()

# SDL3: primero el paquete de CMake; si no está (Linux mínimo), pkg-config.
find_package(SDL3 CONFIG QUIET)
if(SDL3_FOUND)
  target_link_libraries(kult-sdl PRIVATE kultport SDL3::SDL3)
else()
  find_package(PkgConfig REQUIRED)
  pkg_check_modules(SDL3 REQUIRED IMPORTED_TARGET sdl3)
  target_link_libraries(kult-sdl PRIVATE kultport PkgConfig::SDL3)
endif()

# ---- icono de la app (recurso del .exe en Windows) --------------------------
if(WIN32)
  set(KULT_ICON_RC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/kult_icon.rc)
  set(CMAKE_RC_FLAGS "${CMAKE_RC_FLAGS} -I\"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets\"")
  # windres referencia el .ico por ruta; sin esto, regenerarlo no recompila el
  # recurso y el .exe se queda con el icono anterior.
  set_property(SOURCE ${KULT_ICON_RC} PROPERTY OBJECT_DEPENDS
               ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/kult_icon.ico)
  target_sources(kult-sdl PRIVATE ${KULT_ICON_RC})
  set_target_properties(kult-sdl PROPERTIES WIN32_EXECUTABLE TRUE OUTPUT_NAME kult)
  set_target_properties(kult PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME kult-headless)
endif()

# ---- empaquetado de release -------------------------------------------------
# El paquete NO lleva assets del juego: el usuario aporta sus STX en data/.
# kult-headless sigue siendo un target de desarrollo, pero no se empaqueta.
if(APPLE)
  set_target_properties(kult-sdl PROPERTIES
    OUTPUT_NAME "Kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE TRUE
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_INFO_PLIST "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/macos/Info.plist.in"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_BUNDLE_NAME "Kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_GUI_IDENTIFIER "com.hunkstalker.kult"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_ICON_FILE "kult.icns"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_BUNDLE_VERSION "${PROJECT_VERSION}"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_SHORT_VERSION_STRING "${PROJECT_VERSION}"
    MACOSX_BUNDLE_COPYRIGHT "MIT"
    INSTALL_RPATH "@executable_path/../Frameworks")
  if(KULT_SDL3_LIB)
    set(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB "${KULT_SDL3_LIB}")
  else()
    find_library(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB NAMES SDL3 libSDL3.0.dylib)
  endif()
  if(NOT KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB OR NOT EXISTS "${KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB}")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "macOS: define -DKULT_SDL3_LIB=<ruta a libSDL3.0.dylib>")
  endif()
  get_filename_component(KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_REAL "${KULT_SDL3_RUNTIME_LIB}" REALPATH)
endif()

if(APPLE)
  install(TARGETS kult-sdl BUNDLE DESTINATION .)
else()
  install(TARGETS kult-sdl RUNTIME DESTINATION .)
endif()
install(FILES
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/Kult Settings.txt"
  "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/assets/Kult Settings.png"
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/LICENSE

# Core importado y delta del port

El core C vive en `lib/kult-core/`, importado del repositorio
[kult-atari-st-c](https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c) mediante
`git subtree`.

- Última importación: commit `94c0be1` del repo C (T-022; `load_resource_list_c`).
- Importación inicial: commit `beebb52` (subtree con `--squash`).
- El build del port usa `lib/kult-core/src` y `lib/kult-core/include`.
- Las herramientas y tests del core viven también en el subtree.
- No se compilan `lib/kult-core/docs`, `test` ni `tools` salvo que se invoquen
  explícitamente.

## Delta local del port

Estos ficheros del core llevan cambios propios del port:

- `lib/kult-core/src/commands.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/dispatch.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/handlers.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/input.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/loop.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/mode.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/text.c`
- `lib/kult-core/src/video.c`
- `lib/kult-core/include/kult_port.h`

Los cambios son:

1. Instrumentación de diagnóstico (`kult_diag_*`/`kult_text_ev`): llamadas
   acotadas en el core; la implementación vive en `platform/diag.c` y en
   el diferencial son no-op. Ver `DIAGNOSTICO.md`.
2. Espera del sample 0x1f al final de la puerta (`mode.c`), específica del
   timing del port.
3. Hooks/declaraciones no-op para que el core siga compilando sin el port.

## Actualizar desde el repo C

```sh
git subtree pull \
  --prefix=lib/kult-core \
  https://github.com/hunkstalker/kult-atari-st-c.git main \
  --squash
```

Si el pull toca alguno de los ficheros del delta, hay que resolver el conflicto
manteniendo la instrumentación y el shim del port. No se debe borrar el delta
sin revisar antes el comportamiento del port.

## Regenerar

```sh
make addrs
make mapa
make regscan
```

`make addrs` y `make mapa` escriben en `lib/kult-core/include` y
`lib/kult-core/docs/mapa`.
